summary.text: An 85-year-old white man with a history of colon cancer treated by polypectomy and partial colectomy, DVT and PE with an IVC filter, untreated prostate cancer and chronic kidney disease presented with 2 days of chest pain, generalized weakness and mild shortness of breath. Doppler showed a nonocclusive right leg DVT and he was given heparin and admitted to intensive care. Echo and CT showed pericardial and pleural effusions; troponin was negative and PSA was elevated at 17.

He was anemic on examination with hemoglobin 6.7 g/dL, WBC 15.6 and platelets 82. The peripheral smear showed myeloblasts, monoblasts and promonocytes, and the marrow was hypercellular with more than 30% blasts. Flow cytometry showed an abnormal blast population with a monocytic population with aberrant CD56. A diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia with monocytic differentiation and slight plasmacytosis was made; the karyotype was 46,XY with no FISH aberrations, and pleural fluid cytology was considered consistent with leukemic involvement.

After consent he received intramarrow cytarabine, 50 mg/m^(2) into the right posterior ilium, then 30 mg/m^(2) into the sternum three days a week for 2 weeks, without nausea or vomiting. Five days after treatment started, WBC fell to 6.3 and leukemic cells to 40%. The pleural effusion began to regress after 2 weeks and the pericardial effusion regressed completely on CT. Marrow biopsy showed reduced blasts (10%) at about 6 weeks and a normocellular marrow at 18 weeks; blasts of 2.5% were also reported.

He continued to improve clinically but remained mildly leucopenic and thrombocytopenic and became transfusion dependent; the discussion separately reports increasing transfusion dependence about 3 months after therapy, requiring 1–2 units almost every 2 weeks. He became unable to perform activities of daily living, his family declined further transfusion support and chose hospice care, and he died a few days after entering hospice.

ambiguities.issue: Two statements describe transfusion dependence: the case narrative says he became transfusion dependent (no time) and the discussion says about 3 months after therapy he became increasingly transfusion dependent requiring 1–2 units almost every 2 weeks. The source does not say they are the same event, so they are kept as separate facts and events; the cause was "not entirely clear".

ambiguities.issue: The marrow blast and promonocyte (2.5%/1%), plasma cell, light chain and FISH sentences that follow the 6-week and 18-week biopsy sentences state no time themselves; they are plausibly part of the same biopsy reports but the sentences do not say so. The paragraph-final marrow statement in the outcome paragraph (normocellular, trilineage hematopoiesis) likewise has no stated time. These results sit in their own untimed events, not in the dated 6-week and 18-week biopsy events; the 27% promonocyte/monocyte clause is part of the 6-week sentence and keeps that time.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four figure images are reviewed in visual.json.
Graph 1 and Graph 2 print no data labels for the plotted points; only the axes, the "Day of Ara-C injection" marker and qualitative trends are recorded, and marrow values come from the text only.

Discussion paragraphs are mechanism, literature and cited-case commentary and are not index-patient facts; the reference to a previous intramarrow case and a published CLL patient are not index-patient facts.
No reference ranges or high/low flags are printed for the laboratory values; none were inferred (only PSA is called elevated by the source).
Several result sentences follow a dated biopsy or count sentence without a time of their own; no time is borrowed for them (see ambiguities).
The "10^(9)/L" unit is kept as printed; hemoglobin, platelet and WBC values carry no source flag.
